method: Read from the release file by Claude Opus 5.5: the zotero://meet-awesome-gpt handler (doAction), decryptCode and getAesKey; then read the same handler in 3.1.200, the version its update channel serves.
label: A zotero:// link (a web page can open one) can make it run anyone's code without asking you
summary: Its zotero://meet-awesome-gpt link runs the JavaScript it carries, after decrypting it with a key made from a phrase written into the plugin, so anyone who reads the plugin can make a working link and any web page can open it. Version 3.1.200, which Zotero updates it to from Gitee, no longer runs code from this link: it only opens the item a citation link points to.

facts.handler: zotero://meet-awesome-gpt, registered when the plugin starts; reads iv and data from the link
facts.check: none that proves who made the link: data is decrypted with AES-GCM under a key that is the SHA-256 of a phrase written into the plugin, so the same key is in every copy
facts.runs: new AsyncFunction("Zotero", "window", source) with Zotero's full privileges, no prompt
facts.replay: no expiry, nonce or origin check
facts.laterVersions: 3.1.200 (sha256 29f0be7a437d304768e866db37e3bdcf4d24e6f21ebf636b37cfe875ad8c7b3f, from the Gitee update channel) keeps the handler and the phrase but accepts only a canvas-citation JSON or a Zotero.Reader.open(id, {position}) string matched by a regular expression, and opens that item; anything else is rejected. The scanner stops flagging this handler from 3.1.181.
facts.notes: The finding's other link, zotero://ztoolkit-debug, asks before running code. The developer was asked on 2026-11-03 to replace the GitHub release file (MuiseDestiny/zotero-gpt#526).
